newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says tax collection to be tougher.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says tax collection to be tougher.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Thursday that the administration would get tough with collecting taxes.
"We will force everyone to pay taxes -- enterprises, famous politicians and businessmen," Yeltsin said in an annual address to both houses of parliament.
"This means we will boost tax collection, treasury income, give a stimulus to industrial output and that means for economic growth," he said.
Government revenues have been hit by a widespread failure to pay taxes, forcing the government in turn to hold back spending, even on salaries.
The revenues shortfall has also led the International Monetary Fund to repeatedly delay monthly disbursements of its $10 billion loan to Russia.
Yeltsin called for approval of a new tax code, which will create a more equitable tax burden, as soon as possible.
The Russian government has nearly finished drafting a new tax code which will be submitted to the State Duma lower house of parliament in the next few weeks, he said.
